question.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)
$$

Let $F(x)=-4x$ for $x\in [-\pi ,\pi ).$ The Fourier series of the $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${b}_{2}.$

${b}_{2}=$ {{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the sine coefficients are given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{L}x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=\pi $ and $f(x)=-4x$ for $x\in (-\pi ,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{2} & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(-4x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{\pi }x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(-4x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=-4x\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=-4 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\, & ⇒\,v=-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{2} & =\frac{1}{\pi }(uv\,{|}_{-\pi }^{\pi }-{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }(-\frac{1}{2}{[(-4x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)]}_{-\pi }^{\pi }-{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x))(-4)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }(-\frac{1}{2}((-4\pi )\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )-(4\pi )\operatorname{cos}⁡(-2\pi ))-2{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }(-\frac{1}{2}((-4\pi )\cdot 1-(4\pi )\cdot 1)-2\cdot \frac{1}{2}{[\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)]}_{-\pi }^{\pi }) \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }(4\pi -(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-2\pi ))) \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }\cdot (4\pi -0) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
